planting.note: Set out rooted cuttings or nursery plants after soil has warmed and frost danger has passed.

directions: Unlike the common white-flowered form, this selection carries deep violet-purple velvety calyces and corollas for a nearly solid-purple flower spike. Give it full sun and lean, well-drained soil, since rich wet ground produces floppy growth and fewer flower spikes. It stays shrubby through summer and puts on its heaviest bloom as days shorten in late summer and fall, drawing in hummingbirds and late-season pollinators. In marginal zones treat it as a root-hardy perennial and cut the woody stems back hard after a killing frost.

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in spring into sharply drained soil; avoid winter planting in heavy or wet ground.

directions: This selection produces an especially saturated, luminous blue-violet flower color on compact mounds of narrow gray-green foliage. Plant in full sun with excellent drainage, since this California foothill native resents summer irrigation and heavy clay. Shear spent flower spikes back by half after the first bloom flush to tidy the mound and coax out a second round of color into early summer. It is naturally short-lived in garden conditions, so take cuttings every year or two to keep plants vigorous.
